clue.text: It states rules about toilet outside one country house

indicators.note: turning something about faces it the other way, so the toilet's abbreviation is read backwards
one thing standing outside another surrounds it, so the toilet letters go round the rest

blocks.note: WC, water closet, the standard abbreviation for a toilet
the Roman numeral for one
a villa is a large house in the country

explanation.surface: A notice about the toilet stuck up outside a stately home sets out the house rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It states rules' looks like a description of a notice, but it is the definition: the law that states lay down. WC, water closet, is the usual British abbreviation for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil law is the body of legal rules a state lays down governing private matters between citizens.

clue.text: Large-scale constants of mathematics and physics

blocks.note: e, the base of natural logarithms, a mathematical constant
pi, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
c, the speed of light, the best-known constant in physics

explanation.surface: A grand claim about the fundamental constants that underpin maths and physics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constants of mathematics' supplies two famous constants, e and pi; physics adds c, the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epic is grand in scope or scale, like a sweeping film or saga.

clue.text: Almost look upon arbitrator to break agreement?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for look is dropped

blocks.note: to gaze is to look steadily
short for umpire, who arbitrates a match

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the arbitrator with suspicion as a deal threatens to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upon' puts the first piece above the second. To gazump is a British property term: a seller accepts a higher offer after agreeing a price with someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazumping means a seller reneging on an agreed house sale for a better bid, so it breaks an agreement.

clue.text: Dwelling in Cape Cruz finally getting fortune up front

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the place name just before it
a dwelling placed in something sits inside it, between the cape and the closing letter
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word for fortune is read backwards

blocks.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
a hut is a simple dwelling
the last letter of Cruz
hap is an old word for luck or fortune

explanation.surface: Someone living on Cape Cruz strikes it rich and flaunts their luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' looks like 'in advance', but 'up' reverses the fortune and 'front' alone is the definition, meaning nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Front, like nerve or cheek, means brazen audacity, which is exactly what chutzpah is.

clue.text: One expected to make final over tried to run

indicators.note: letters set to run scatter out of position and reassemble in a new order

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer tries to run out one last over to reach the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make final' sounds like reaching a cup final; it really means giving copy its final form.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the person who decides on the final version of a text or film before it is published.

clue.text: Hello!, say, causes weeping for some

blocks.note: first meaning: a salutation, of which hello is an example
second meaning: in Scots, to greet is to cry, so some speakers use the word for weeping

explanation.surface: A simple hello moves some people to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some' signals a regional usage: in Scotland greeting means crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting is a word of welcome such as hello, and in Scottish dialect it also means crying.

clue.text: Shelly caught boss losing head over heartless model

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for boss is dropped
with no heart, the centre letter of the word for model goes

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a honcho is the boss, the person in charge
an ideal is a model to be imitated

explanation.surface: A boss named Shelly gets caught out after an affair with a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelly' looks like a woman's name but is the adjective: like a shell. 'over' places the first pieces above the last in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Conchoidal describes a curved, shell-like surface, as on fractured flint, so it means shell-shaped or shelly.

clue.text: Discovered heater on railway diner

indicators.note: dis-covered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the heater go

blocks.note: taken as written
RY is the standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone finds a heater on board the railway dining car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but split as dis-covered it removes H and R from heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is an informal restaurant, and an eatery is any place serving food to customers.

clue.text: Found fault with fruit–half returned for wrapping

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for half is read backwards
a wrapping goes around its contents, so the reversed half encloses the fruit

blocks.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half
a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone complains about fruit that came back half wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: IMED, demi reversed, splits around PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to accuse or call into question, so impeached means challenged or found fault with.

clue.text: Wine or port served before Munich Agreement

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
ja is German for yes, the way agreement is said in Munich

explanation.surface: A drinks choice: wine, or port served before the historic 1938 Munich Agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Munich Agreement is the 1938 pact, but here it means saying yes in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish wine from the region of that name.

clue.text: Wrapped in this month’s vintage coat

indicators.note: something wrapped in another thing is enclosed by it, so the vintage goes inside

blocks.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters
a cru is a wine growth or vintage

explanation.surface: Someone is wrapped up in this month's vintage-style coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To incrust is to cover with a hard outer layer, so as a verb it means coat.

clue.text: Sentimentality born of Electra complex

indicators.note: complex means intricately tangled, so the letters of the name are muddled together

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mawkish feeling explained as the product of a daughter's Electra complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electra complex' is a real psychological term, which disguises 'complex' as part of a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is figuratively cloying, overly sweet sentiment, just as the syrup is sickly sweet.

clue.text: Scoop secured by conceited young man from Hollywood?

blocks.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, LA
a pup is an arrogant, cheeky young man

explanation.surface: A cocky young Hollywood type lands a big scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Hollywood' puts LA before the young man, as in an LA pup.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoop up eagerly, like a cat with milk, is to lap up something offered.

clue.text: Animal display that is at last filmed to fill TV slot

indicators.note: at last directs us to the final letter of the following word
filling a slot means going inside it, so the other pieces sit within the slot word

blocks.note: to air something is to display it publicly
i.e., id est, means that is
the last letter of filmed
prog is short for a television programme

explanation.surface: A wildlife show finally gets filmed to fill a television slot.
explanation.walkthrough: Prog is informal British shorthand for a TV or radio programme, and 'display' is the verb sense of putting something on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie dog is a burrowing rodent of North American grasslands, an animal related to squirrels.

clue.text: Closeness of singer-songwriter in timeless gathering

indicators.note: timeless means without time, so the letter standing for time is removed
the singer is placed in the gathering, inside its remaining letters

blocks.note: Paul Simon, the American singer-songwriter
a party is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A close bond with a singer-songwriter forms at a gathering that seems to stand outside time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closeness' tempts toward intimacy, but here it means stinginess. T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness can mean meanness with money, being close-fisted, and parsimony is extreme reluctance to spend.

clue.text: Baathists endlessly weighed up a question when confused?

indicators.note: without an end, the final letter of the party members' name is cut
things that are up in the air are in disorder, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written; Baathists belong to the Arab Baath party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Baath party members ponder a question while in a state of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weighed up' reads as considered, but 'up' is the anagram signal applied to BAATHIST plus WEIGHED.
explanation.definitionFit: What's the big idea? is an indignant question asked by someone baffled by another person's behaviour.

clue.text: Rage and refuse to go under sail

blocks.note: to storm is to rage
a horse that jibs refuses to go on

explanation.surface: Someone rages and refuses to set out under sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm jib is a small, strong triangular headsail used by yachts in heavy weather.

clue.text: Launch the ultimate in entertainment

indicators.note: placed in the word for entertainment, the ultimate sits inside it

blocks.note: boff is slang for a hearty laugh or a hit show
the ultimate thing is the last one

explanation.surface: A boast that this show is the very best in entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate in entertainment' reads as the best show around, but 'in' is a placement instruction. Boff is mainly American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast-off is the moment a rocket leaves the ground, its launch.

clue.text: Classified advertisement about fancy stores

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, inviting the letters to be rearranged
about means around, so the advertisement surrounds the rearranged letters

blocks.note: ad is short for advertisement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A classified ad promoting fancy shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classified advertisement' is a familiar phrase, but 'Classified' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted things have been sorted into groups, which is what classified means.

clue.text: Mostly tough girl donates an organ

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter of the word for tough goes

blocks.note: hard means tough
Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tough girl generously donates an organ for transplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a body part, but here it is a mouth organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is also called a mouth organ, a small instrument played by blowing through reeds.

clue.text: Point in uppermost part of the Pleiades, for example

indicators.note: the point is placed in the word for uppermost part, sitting inside it

blocks.note: the head is the top part
pt is an abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: Pointing to the top of the Pleiades star cluster in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pleiades are popularly called the Seven Sisters, which makes them a group of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a group of seven, and the Pleiades are traditionally seven stars or sisters.

clue.text: Turned out kids regularly with most of their skin

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
most of means nearly all, so the last letter of the skin word goes

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of kids
suede is the skin of kids, young goats, used as leather

explanation.surface: Children turned out in regular fashion wearing nearly all their skins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their skin' fits because suede is often kidskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Issued means sent out or put forth, as a statement or uniform is turned out to people.

clue.text: Scrapes line in scraping tools

indicators.note: the line is put in the word for scraping tools, sitting inside it

blocks.note: hoes are garden tools used to scrape weeds
L is an abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A gardener's scraping tools leave a line of scrapes in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapes' looks like a verb but means awkward predicaments.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, and being in a hole means the same kind of trouble.

clue.text: Breaking shopaholic’s heart is fair game

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the word are kept
breaking something smashes it apart, so its letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the central six letters of shopaholic

explanation.surface: Someone who breaks a compulsive shopper's heart is treated as fair game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair game' reads as a legitimate target, but here it is a game at a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground game in which players throw rings over prizes to win them.

clue.text: Power is inclined to suppress what’s right in morale boosters

indicators.note: what is at the right-hand end of a word is its last letter
suppressing something holds it down inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
something that ramps slopes or is inclined
the last letter of morale

explanation.surface: Those in power are inclined to crush whatever is good for morale.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside RAMPS after the R, giving P + R-E-AMPS. 'morale boosters' is a stock phrase that hides the split before 'boosters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Preamps are preamplifiers, which boost a weak audio signal before the main amplifier.

clue.text: In which you’d often edit help file?

definitions.text: In which you’d often edit help file?

blocks.clueFragment: In which you’d often edit help file?
blocks.note: surface reading: where you might go to revise a help document
setter's reading: Edit, Help and File are menu names found in a strip of buttons at the top of a program window

explanation.surface: Someone asks where they would usually revise a help document.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'edit', 'help' and 'file' not as an action and object but as three menu labels found side by side in software.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolbar is the strip of a software window holding menus such as File, Edit and Help.

clue.text: Fluffy scarf found on black tropical tree

blocks.note: a boa is a long fluffy scarf of feathers or fur
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A feather boa turns up on a black tree in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The boab is the Australian baobab, a tropical tree with a massive swollen trunk.

clue.text: Boxer once touring west of Ireland, round Mayo, in part?

indicators.note: the west of a word, read left to right, is its first letter
touring means travelling around, so the boxer's name goes around the other letters

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, the former heavyweight champion
the first letter of Ireland
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A former boxer tours the west of Ireland, travelling round County Mayo.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayo looks like the Irish county, but it is short for mayonnaise; the question mark marks the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise, so it is one kind among the family of mayo sauces.

clue.text: Make outside shed

blocks.note: surface reading: build a garden shed outdoors
setter's reading: cause the outer surface to come off in flakes

explanation.surface: An instruction to build a shed out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a noun for a garden hut, but it is a verb: make the outside layer drop off.
explanation.definitionFit: To exfoliate is to remove dead outer cells or scales, making the surface layer peel away.
